en: To Arjuna, overwhelmed by pity, his eyes full of tears and his heart sinking, Madhusudana spoke these words.
speaker: Sanjaya said

en: Arjuna, where has this weakness come from at such a moment? It does not befit a noble person, and it leads neither to heaven nor to honour.
speaker: Krishna said

sa: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते।
tr: klaibyaṃ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitattvayyupapadyate
en: Do not give in to this unmanliness, Partha; it does not suit you. Throw off this petty weakness of heart and stand up, scorcher of foes.

sa: कथं भीष्ममहं संख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन।
tr: kathaṃ bhīṣmamahaṃ saṃkhye droṇaṃ ca madhusūdana
en: Madhusudana, how can I shoot arrows in battle at Bhishma and Drona? They deserve my reverence, slayer of foes.
speaker: Arjuna said

en: It would be better to live in this world on alms than to kill these noble teachers. If I killed them, every pleasure and every gain I enjoyed here would be stained with blood.

sa: यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः।
tr: yadvā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ
en: We do not even know which is better for us, that we conquer them or that they conquer us. The sons of Dhritarashtra stand before us; if we kill them, we would not want to live.
My nature is overcome by weakness and pity, and my mind is confused about my duty. I ask you: tell me for certain what is best. I am your disciple and I have come to you for refuge. Teach me.
I see nothing that could drive away this grief that is drying up my senses, not even an unrivalled, prosperous kingdom on earth or lordship over the gods.

sa: न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह ॥
tr: na yotsya iti govindamuktvā tūṣṇīṃ babhūva ha
en: Having said this to Krishna, Arjuna, the scorcher of foes, told Govinda, "I will not fight," and fell silent.
speaker: Sanjaya said

en: Then, between the two armies, Krishna, as if smiling, spoke these words to the grieving Arjuna.
You grieve for those who need no grief, and yet you speak words that sound wise. The wise grieve neither for the living nor for the dead.
speaker: Krishna said

sa: न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः।
न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम् ॥
tr: na tvevāhaṃ jātu nāsaṃ na tvaṃ neme janādhipāḥ
na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayamataḥ param
en: There was never a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor these kings; and there will never be a time when any of us ceases to be.
Just as the soul passes through childhood, youth and old age in this body, so it passes into another body. The steady are not confused by this.
Contact of the senses with their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and do not last. Bear them patiently, Arjuna.

sa: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ।
tr: yaṃ hi na vyathayantyete puruṣaṃ puruṣarṣabha
en: The person these do not disturb, who stays the same in pleasure and pain, steady and wise, is fit for immortality.

sa: नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः।
tr: nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ
en: The unreal never comes to be, and the real never stops being. Those who see the truth have understood both.

sa: अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्।
tr: avināśi tu tadviddhi yena sarvamidaṃ tatam
en: Know that what pervades this whole body is indestructible. No one can destroy what is imperishable.
These bodies of the eternal, indestructible and immeasurable soul are said to come to an end. Therefore fight, Arjuna.

sa: य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम्।
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते ॥
tr: ya enaṃ vetti hantāraṃ yaścainaṃ manyate hatam
ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate
en: One who thinks the soul is a killer, and one who thinks it is killed, both fail to understand. It neither kills nor is killed.

sa: न्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः।
tr: nnāyaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ
en: The soul is never born and never dies. It did not come into being and will not stop being. Unborn, eternal, everlasting and ancient, it is not killed when the body is killed.

sa: कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम् ॥
tr: kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha kaṃ ghātayati hanti kam
en: Partha, how could one who knows the soul to be indestructible, eternal, unborn and unchanging kill anyone, or make anyone kill?
Just as a person throws away worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, the soul throws away worn-out bodies and enters new ones.

sa: नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः।
न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः ॥
tr: nainaṃ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ
na cainaṃ kledayantyāpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ
en: Weapons cannot cut it, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it and wind cannot dry it.
It cannot be cut, burned, wetted or dried. It is eternal, present everywhere, stable, unmoving and timeless.
It is called unmanifest, beyond thought and unchanging. Knowing it to be so, you should not grieve.

sa: अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम्।
tr: atha cainaṃ nityajātaṃ nityaṃ vā manyase mṛtam
en: And even if you think the soul is constantly born and constantly dies, mighty-armed one, you still have no reason to grieve.

sa: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च।
tr: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyurdhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca
en: Death is certain for whoever is born, and birth is certain for whoever dies. So you should not grieve over what cannot be avoided.
Beings are unmanifest before birth, manifest in the middle, and unmanifest again at death. What is there to mourn, Arjuna?
Some see the soul as a wonder, some speak of it as a wonder, and some hear of it as a wonder; yet even after hearing, no one truly knows it.
The soul that lives in every body can never be killed, Arjuna. So you should not grieve for any being.
Considering your own duty as well, you should not waver. For a warrior there is nothing better than a war fought for what is right.
Fortunate are the warriors, Partha, to whom such a war comes unsought, like an open door to heaven.

sa: अथ चैत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि।
ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
tr: atha caittvamimaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ na kariṣyasi
tataḥ svadharmaṃ kīrtiṃ ca hitvā pāpamavāpsyasi
en: But if you refuse to fight this righteous war, you will give up your duty and your honour, and you will incur sin.
People will tell of your disgrace for ever, and for someone who has been honoured, disgrace is worse than death.

sa: येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम् ॥
tr: yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ bahumato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam
en: The great warriors will think you fled the battle out of fear, and those who held you in high regard will think little of you.

sa: निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम् ॥
tr: nindantastava sāmarthyaṃ tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim
en: Your enemies will say many unspeakable things, mocking your strength. What could be more painful than that?

sa: हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्।
tr: hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṃ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm
en: If you are killed, you will reach heaven; if you win, you will enjoy the earth. So stand up, son of Kunti, determined to fight.
Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat alike, get ready for battle. That way you will incur no sin.

sa: एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां श्रृणु।
tr: eṣā te'bhihitā sāṃkhye buddhiryoge tvimāṃ śrṛṇu
en: I have explained this wisdom to you in terms of Sankhya; now hear it in terms of yoga. United with this understanding, Partha, you will break the bonds of karma.
On this path no effort is ever wasted and no harm is done. Even a little of this practice protects you from great fear.
Here the determined mind is focused on one thing, Arjuna; the thoughts of the undetermined are endless and branch in every direction.
Those without discernment speak in flowery words, delighting in the letter of the Vedas and saying there is nothing more, Partha.
Full of desires and intent on heaven, they recommend many elaborate rites aimed at pleasure and power, which only bring rebirth as the fruit of action.
For those attached to pleasure and power, whose minds are carried away by such talk, the determined, focused mind does not arise in meditation.
The Vedas deal with the three qualities of nature. Rise above them, Arjuna: free from the pairs of opposites, always grounded in truth, unconcerned with getting and keeping, and centred in the Self.
To someone who knows Brahman, all the Vedas are as useful as a small pond in a land flooded with water on every side.
You have a right to your work, but never to its fruits. Do not let the fruits of action be your motive, and do not cling to inaction either.

sa: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
tr: yogasthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dhanañjaya
siddhyasiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṃ yoga ucyate
en: Do your work grounded in yoga, Dhananjaya, letting go of attachment and staying even-minded in success and failure. This evenness of mind is called yoga.
Work done for its rewards is far below work guided by wisdom, Dhananjaya. Take refuge in that wisdom; those who work only for the fruits are to be pitied.
One united with this wisdom leaves behind both good and bad deeds even in this life. So commit yourself to yoga: yoga is skill in action.

sa: कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः।
tr: karmajaṃ buddhiyuktā hi phalaṃ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ
en: The wise, united with this understanding, let go of the fruits of action, are freed from the bonds of birth, and reach the state beyond all sorrow.

sa: तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥
tr: tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca
en: When your understanding crosses the swamp of delusion, you will no longer care about what you have heard or what is still to be heard.
When your understanding, unsettled by conflicting teachings, stands firm and unmoving in meditation, you will reach yoga.

sa: स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम् ॥
tr: sthitadhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣeta kimāsīta vrajeta kim
en: Keshava, how would you describe someone whose wisdom is steady and who is absorbed in meditation? How does such a person speak, sit and walk?
speaker: Arjuna said

sa: प्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनोगतान्।
tr: prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha manogatān
en: When a person lets go of every desire of the mind, Partha, and is content in the Self through the Self, they are said to have steady wisdom.
speaker: Krishna said

en: One who is not shaken by sorrow, does not long for pleasure, and is free from attachment, fear and anger is called a sage of steady mind.

sa: नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
tr: nābhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
en: One who is unattached everywhere, who neither celebrates good fortune nor resents bad, has wisdom that is firmly established.
When, like a tortoise drawing in its limbs, a person withdraws the senses from their objects, their wisdom is firmly established.
Sense objects fall away from one who abstains from them, but the taste for them remains; even that taste disappears once the Supreme is seen.
The restless senses, son of Kunti, can forcibly carry away the mind even of a wise person who is striving for control.

sa: तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः।
वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
tr: tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya yukta āsīta matparaḥ
vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
en: Restraining them all, one should sit in yoga, devoted to Me. Whoever has their senses under control has steady wisdom.
When a person dwells on sense objects, attachment to them grows; from attachment comes desire, and from desire comes anger.
From anger comes delusion; from delusion, a confused memory; from a confused memory, the loss of reason; and when reason is lost, the person is ruined.
But a disciplined person who moves among sense objects with senses under control, free from attraction and aversion, reaches inner calm.
In that calm all sorrows come to an end, and the understanding of the calm-hearted quickly becomes steady.
One who is not disciplined has no wisdom and no focus; without focus there is no peace, and without peace, how can there be happiness?
Just as a strong wind sweeps a boat off course on the water, a mind that follows the wandering senses carries away one's wisdom.
So, mighty-armed one, the person whose senses are fully withdrawn from their objects has wisdom that is firmly established.

sa: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी।
यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥
tr: yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī
yasyāṃ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ
en: What is night for all beings is wakefulness for the self-disciplined; and what is wakefulness for all beings is night for the sage who truly sees.
Just as the ocean stays full and still while rivers keep flowing into it, the person into whom desires flow in the same way finds peace, not the one who chases desires.
Whoever lets go of all desires and lives free from longing, without the sense of "mine" and without ego, finds peace.

sa: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति।
tr: eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṃ prāpya vimuhyati
en: This is the state of Brahman, Partha. Having reached it, one is no longer deluded; established in it even at the time of death, one attains the peace of Brahman.
